title: Inkwell Markets on‑prem prototype jot
content:
Call notes (2026-03-03) with Inkwell Markets — initial on‑prem prototype followup

Attendees: Jordan (Redwood SE), Maya (Redwood Solutions), Priya (Redwood PM), Tom H. (Inkwell infra lead), Saira B. (Inkwell quant), Leo (Inkwell security)

High-level ask
- Inkwell wants a low-latency, private deployment of a trading assistant model that can:
  - score and rerank signal candidates in <= 30ms p50 on short sequences (<=64 tokens)
  - support 500 concurrent QPS during market open burst windows
  - keep all PII and internal data on-prem, integrate with their HSM for key management

What we demo'd / tried in sandbox
- Lightweight on‑prem control plane (private control plane pattern) using a user-provided bastion + Redwood agent.
- Model variants: distilled 7B float16 and 4-bit quantized 13B — tradeoff notes: 7B hits latency target but occasional hallucinations on domain-specific prompt tokens; 13B-4bit better quality but needs ~10ms extra compute.
- KV prefix cache configured for common market templates — cut token cost by ~22% in synthetic traces.

Primary technical constraints mentioned by Inkwell
- Strict egress: only outbound to Redwood control plane on port 443 allowed (TLS), no inbound allowed except via bastion.
- HSM cert rotation every 48h — ask: how to automate rotated key pickup in agent without human step?
- Compliance wants per-request audit logs, immutably shipped to their Splunk cluster.

Gotchas / risks we identified
- Network hop variability: their private colo had 3-6ms jitter during heavy trading tests; this will eat into our 30ms p50 SLO. Need to simulate real burst jitter.
- Quantization non-determinism: some rerank edge-cases move items across the decision boundary with quantized kernels. Need targeted evals on their prompt set.
- Cold KV cache misses at market open can spike latency — autoscaler + warmup strategy required.
- HSM agent permission model: if agent runs as root vs restricted user it affects HSM driver compatibility (Linux distro differences, they use Rocky 8).

Unresolved questions from the call
1) Can Inkwell provide a 48‑hour representative trace of token length distribution and QPS (anonymized)? They said maybe — follow up with legal.
2) Are there internal feature flags that mutate prompt templates at runtime? If yes, we need hooks to invalidate cached prefixes.
3) Will the Splunk ingestion accept batched audit events or only single-request logs?

Short-term technical experiments to run (Redwood + Inkwell)
- (Jordan) Run a 2-hour latency jitter test from Inkwell colo into our agent image to measure p50/p95 impact with 0/1/2 ms artificial jitter. Ticket: JIRA-INK-143. Target: 2026-03-10.
- (Maya + Alexei) Build a small eval harness that runs Inkwell's seed prompt set against quantized 13B and distilled 7B. Metric: rerank AUC + hallucination flag rate. Deliverable: short report. Target: 2026-03-14.
- (Priya) Draft key rotation flow for HSM integration — two variants: pull via agent with secure token vending, or push certs to agent via internal orchestration. Need legal input on pull pattern. Target: 2026-03-09.

Configuration notes (for infra)
- Agent container: non-root user preferred; include libhsm driver v2.1 for their Nitro HSM shim.
- Runtime settings: prefer dynamic batching disabled for latency-critical routes; set max_batch_size=8, batch_timeout_ms=6 for their traffic profile.
- KV cache: per-customer namespace, LRU with 10k entries, TTL 12h but invalidate on template-change webhook.
- Autoscaler: maintain baseline of 6 inference workers across availability slots, add burst instances with warmup strategy (preload KV & model into GPU memory).

Security & compliance bits
- Audit trail: include request_id, model_version, user_token_hash (not raw token), HSM_key_id, response_hash. Ship via signed envelope to their Splunk endpoint.
- Data residency: confirm log retention policy — they require 90-day retrievability, then 365-day archive on cold storage.
- Pen test: Inkwell expects a lightweight network pentest for the agent image before prod rollout. Schedule window after agent build.

Notes to self (fragmented)
- Tom sounded worried about vendor lock — emphasize we support model pinning + bring-your-own-model variants in the runbook.
- Mention Redwood Optimize suggestions: recommend quantization+KV combo for cost predictability; include case study notes for a similar hedge-fund pilot (internal doc id GH:repo/case-studies#22).
- Need to keep one pager that compares: 7B float16 vs 13B-4bit vs hosted fallback (latency and p95 cost).

Next steps & owners
- Jordan: gather estimator for cost per 1M tokens & expected infra baseline cost for their QPS profile. (Due 2026-03-12)
- Maya: run eval harness & deliver initial quality comparison (Due 2026-03-14)
- Priya: finalize HSM rotation proposal + compliance checklist (Due 2026-03-09)
- Tom (Inkwell): check with legal on anonymized trace share and Splunk ingestion format (Due 2026-03-06)

Meeting follow-up items to include in email recap
- Short summary of latency tradeoffs and proposed config (batching disabled, small batch_size, prewarmed pool).
- Attach eval plan + list of prompts we will run.
- Ask for environment details: OS/kernel, NIC model, top-of-rack switch, firewall egress rules.
- Proposed timeline for 1-week onprem pilot (staging -> limited prod)

Random brainstorm (for internal discussion)
- Could we ship a minimal 'KV-warmup' endpoint that Inkwell can call a minute before market open to prepopulate cache across workers? This would reduce cold-miss spikes.
- Explore falling back to a small hosted microservice for rerank pass only if local latency > threshold — but watch out for egress policy.

End of note.

Quick revision log:
- 2026-03-05: added HSM rotation tasks and updated owners (Jordan)
- 2026-03-03: initial call notes captured
